caption: The drawing depicts an interior room with a green floor and green walls accented by blue and purple decorative borders near the ceiling. There are several large, grey columns with ornate capitals supporting the ceiling, spaced throughout the space. Five lamp posts, topped with four-globed lamps, stand between the columns, each decorated with a large black ribbon. In the foreground, there are rows of white wicker chairs, some with black fabric draped over them. Arranged on one of the chairs is a tray with a cup, a plate, a folded newspaper, and a book. An open book and a round white object rest on another chair, alongside a black hat with a purple ribbon labeled "HUSBAND" and a crochet item. Further back, a black wood stove is positioned on the left, with a standing black umbrella leaning nearby and some firewood beneath it. Metal stands, floral arrangements, and wreaths populate the background and mid-ground. The most prominent wreath is mounted on a stand and has purple ribbons reading "GONE BUT NOT FORGOTTEN." A framed painting with blue, green, and white colors is centered on the back wall, flanked by smaller decorative stands and more floral tributes. Doves are perched on some objects, including one on the wreath, and one flying white dove is depicted mid-air. On the left, through an open doorway, a black horse-drawn hearse is visible outside. On the right, another room can be partially seen, featuring a mantelpiece and a wreath inscribed "IN MEMORY OF." The ceilings are painted light blue. The entire composition employs a limited color palette focused on greens, blues, greys, black, purple, and white.
title: Funeral Parlor, 1895-1920
